comment: Bad-mannered, foul-mouthed, hot-tempered punk rocker and wannabe anarchist. Doesn't seem to pay much attention to politics, rather concentrating on cheap beer, bad vodka and two-chord choruses. Lousy on the guitar, but compensates with loads of enthusiasm.

Anarchist punk rocker with wet dreams of the revolution, when the weak will take power. Also an animal-rights-activist and a vegan. Happily fights police, as they represent the oppressing state. Rather a musical talent, skilled at playing both bass and guitar.

Really big in the sixties. Began drinking when his career went down the drain, but after a few decades of anonymity he returned to the stage and to everyone's surprise his comeback tour was sold out. Never big with the critics, his fans are mid-fifties and dream of lost youth.

Small towner who spent most of his adolescence in the garage playing distorted guitar as loud as possible. Moved to Rock City at age fifteen and has played guitar in numerous bands by now. Really skilled at playing the three chords he knows and looks good on stage.

Teddy probably will never win the Nobel prize, but on bass he's as steady as a rock in any band. Prefers the simple to the overly complicated and likes to play it loud. He's content most of the time and likes to party hard. Also a big motor fan.

Conrad is a preppy boy who puts two things first in life: his guitar Mandy and his collection of old pop bootlegs. Likes to be seen with the right crowd and is very careful with his appearance. Some call him snob, but Conny prefers to call himself "selective". Control-freak.

Hotheaded lady whose temper has gotten her in trouble more than once. Corky will never be one for tricky rhythm switches, but compensates by beating the drums harder than anyone else. Her arms often cramp, resulting in slower tempo towards the end of the songs.

More or less born with a bass guitar in his hand. Also a decent keyboard player. Chris is an often hired session musician and has a much appreciated streak to his personality: he has no wish for stardom, he just likes to play the bass real loud.

A skilled and experienced vocalist, Sharon had her own band in the eighties and had a few minor hits, but the band never really broke. She's been singing all types of music, but her heart is definitely in straight-forward easy-to-swallow radio rock.

Trina is a small-towner gone metropolitan. She's been playing guitar and singing in different bands to fight the small town dreariness. She's independent and rather decisive. She spends her spare time writing bad poetry about gray skies and lost love.

Talented vocalist with a good, strong voice that fits nicely in most contexts. Also a skilled keyboard player. Some say that she is difficult to work with and suggest she's a bit of a diva. Diva or not, Mary usually gets what she wants.

Front man who lives for evil metal with battle-axe riffs and double bass drums. Doesn't mind electronic machinery as long as the PTA are still upset. Jamie wants to be bad, but the truth is that he prefers computer games to drugs. Has a schizo streak.

Decent bass player with star quality and a good stage appearance. Likes to party and is easy to work with most of the time. Very serious about her music, yet hungry for stardom. Perfect for your desktop band  mould her into any form you choose.

A cocky kid with loads of attitude, off and on stage. Critics agree that he's a radiant stage persona. Lol is very moody and hopeless to work with, which his brother Nelly can testify to. However, it's only with Nelly's music that Lol gets his act together and does his extraordinary best.

Raised in New York and London, Mark has got the latest dance floor beats all figured out. This kid is underground avantgarde, always on the front edge of dance music development. Prefers to stay home to work on his beats to doing live gigs.

Roy likes to get attention and he doesn't really care how. He loves the limelight and from time to time he has to be forced off stage. Has trouble dividing his time between music and women. Charming but very obsessive.

Raymond is a semi-celebrity in the gay community after his time as a drummer with Neon Studs in the eighties. The rough years in the lower divisions of show biz has made its marks, and Raymond is prone to powdering his nose a bit too much. At those times, he is a pain to deal with.

A vocalist who believes himself to be God's gift to both music and women. On stage (mostly pub gigs), Roberto likes to delve into soulful interpretations of old romantic ballads. He has a somewhat unrealistic view of himself as a singer and a ladies' man.

Matt rides a skateboard and is one of the kindest persons on the planet. He's a vegetarian, a non-smoker, non-drinker, drug-free and likes animals. He's down with the straight edge thing, but thinks it's unnecessary to shout so much.

Lucy makes a lot of young boys' hearts beat faster, standing behind her bass guitar, smiling her enigmatic introvert smile. Maybe it's her melancholy, maybe it's her way of playing a funky bass line without losing her suave and distant appeal. Also plays keyboard.

In the eighties, Eddie was a great sex symbol and stadium rock icon. Among metal fans, he was famous for his fiveandahalf-octave voice span. Some say the success got to Eddie's head, but he onlys shrugs and states that all important artists are controversial.

A great bass player, who in the late eighties developed a taste for controlled substances. Drugs had a bad influence on Andy's unstable psyche and caused several serious depressions. Grew up with Eddie St. Johns.

The readers of Metal Anvil voted Sonny best guitarist in the world for several years in the eighties. He was famous for his speed and ability to mix heavy metal with classical music. Plays with Eddie St. Johns (the frontman of Firewolf), but they don't always get along well.

The drummer of Firewolf and the clown of the band, always playing practical jokes on his bandmates. Manny is happiest after a sweaty gig, drinking copious amounts of beer backstage. Used to be admired by other drummers for his endless solos and double bass drum skills.

Nelly has an outstanding ability to nick melodies from sixties hits and piece them together to suit his brother Lol's voice perfectly. Some claim that Nelly writes the same song over and over, but Nelly says that it doesn't matter since it's the best song in the world.

Nadia is the daughter of business man and entrepreneur Sergey Spektor. She above all wants to be famous, go to glittery premieres and appear on talk shows. Singing seems like a lot of fun, too. As Sergey's daughter she is used to getting what she wants.

Nick has the gift to make the struggle of everyday life into great poetry. After his acclaimed debut album he went incognito and since then media and public have loudly requested a new record. Nick is a double nature who can't stand stardom and yet can't live without music.
